name: Turn one long video into vertical Shorts (Zvid)

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $json.llmModel, response_format: { type: "json_object" }, messages: [ { role: "system", content: "You are a short-form video editor. You return JSON only.\n\nYou never invent words: you only choose ranges of the transcript you are given, by index." }, { role: "user", content: $json.promptText } ] }) }}

parameters.content:
## Long video in, vertical Shorts out

POST a direct video URL to this workflow. It downloads the start of the file,
transcribes it with ElevenLabs **Scribe**, asks an LLM to pick the best
moments, and renders each one as a polished 1080x1920 clip with word-timed
karaoke captions, a title card and a progress hairline — then answers the
webhook with the finished clip URLs.

```
POST http://<your-n8n>/webhook/video-to-shorts
{ "videoUrl": "https://.../talk.mp4", "title": "optional", "layout": "fit | fill" }
```

### Setup (about four minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*,
   *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **ElevenLabs** — add a SECOND **Header Auth** credential: name
   `xi-api-key`, value = your ElevenLabs key. Attach it to
   *Transcribe (Scribe)*. Speech-to-text is billed per minute of audio.
3. **OpenRouter** — add an **OpenRouter** credential and attach it to
   *Pick highlights*. Any JSON-capable model works; the default is
   `google/gemini-2.5-flash`.
4. **Open `Config`** — set `handle` and `brandAccent`.
5. **Run it.** *Test manually* uses the sample video in the *Sample video*
   node so you can see the whole thing work before wiring anything up.
   **The first run renders for real and spends credits — about 28 per 27-second
   clip, so roughly 56 for a default two-clip run.**
6. Free preview first? Set `dryRun: true` in **Config**: you get the exact
   credit quote per clip plus an **editorLink** for each one, nothing spent.

## What you can POST

`videoUrl` must return **the video file itself**, not a watch page.

| Source | What to send |
| --- | --- |
| Your own CDN / S3 / R2 | the object URL |
| Google Drive | the normal share link — *Video request* rewrites it to the `uc?export=download` form for you |
| Dropbox | the share link with `?dl=1` |
| YouTube / Vimeo / TikTok | **not supported** — those are watch pages, not files. Export the video and upload it somewhere that serves the MP4 directly. |

`title` is optional context for the highlight picker. `layout` is optional
and overrides the Config default for that one call.

The manual trigger uses *Sample video* instead of the webhook body, so you
can test the whole chain before pointing anything at n8n.

### Post footage you have the right to post

Every clip renders `handle`, the model-written hook and the transcript over
whoever is on screen. That is fine on your own recording. It is **not** fine
on someone else's: a stranger's face under your handle, or under a hook they
never said, is a false attribution — and a brand's product under an invented
claim is worse. If you are demoing this template with stock or borrowed
footage, use clips with no identifiable faces and no logos, wordmarks or
legible signage in frame, and keep the hook out of the first person.

## Only the downloaded part gets clipped

*Fetch video sample* sends a `Range: bytes=0-…` header capped at
`maxTranscribeMB` (24 MB by default), so a two-hour recording never has to
travel through n8n. MP4 and MP3 tolerate that: the decoder reads what
arrived and stops.

The honest consequence: **clips can only come from the part that was
downloaded.** At 24 MB that is roughly the first 2–6 minutes of a typical
1080p upload, more for a low-bitrate talking-head recording. Raise
`maxTranscribeMB` to reach further in — the cost is transfer time and
ElevenLabs minutes, not credits.

If the file was written with its index (`moov` atom) at the END — some
phone exports and screen recorders do this — a truncated download will not
parse at all and *Read transcript* fails loudly. Re-export with
"fast start" / "web optimised", or raise the cap above the file size.

## How the clips are chosen

*Read transcript* turns Scribe's word list into a numbered transcript:
every 15 words start a new line prefixed with the index of the first word.

*Pick highlights* asks the model for `startWord`/`endWord` INDEX pairs plus
a ≤ 6-word title — never for timestamps. *Prepare clips* maps those indices
back to the real Scribe times, grows or trims each clip one word at a time
until it lands between `minClipSeconds` and `maxClipSeconds`, drops any
overlap, and adds a 0.3 s lead-in and 0.45 s tail.

So the model chooses WHICH words; the arithmetic that decides where the cut
lands is ours. If the model returns nothing usable, the transcript is split
evenly instead and `pickedByModel: false` shows up in the summary — a run
never dies because a model had an off day.

## fit vs fill

This workflow does **not** track faces, so it never guesses where the
subject is.

- **`fit`** (default) — the whole frame is kept and centred, with a
  blurred, darkened copy of the same footage filling the rest of the
  canvas. Two-shots, panels, screen shares and slides all survive.
- **`fill`** — a full-bleed centre crop. Sharper and cheaper to render,
  correct when you know the subject is centred (a single talking head, or
  footage that is already vertical).

Set it in `Config`, or per call in the webhook body.

## One render job per clip

*Build project JSON* emits one item per clip, and every node from there on
runs once per item: N validations, N renders, N jobs polled in the same
loop. *Merge job status* zips each status response back onto its clip by
index, which is safe because Wait passes items through unchanged.

Clips do not finish on the same lap, so *Merge job status* also sets one
`allCompleted` flag on every item and *Render finished?* routes on that.
The batch leaves the loop together and the webhook gets ONE answer listing
every clip, instead of an early partial list.

**Credits scale with clips.** `clipCount: 2` at `clipSeconds: 28` is about
56 credits a run. Drop to `clipCount: 1`, `clipSeconds: 20` for a cheap
test — the validator quotes the exact figure before anything is spent.

## Watching the clips, and shipping them onward

Click **▶ Watch video** after a run: n8n renders each downloaded MP4 as an
inline video player with a download button — one per clip, no URLs to copy.
*Run summary* before it carries `videoUrl`, `title`, `sourceStart` and
`creditsCharged` per clip if you want to pipe the result onward.

### Publishing (optional tail)

The workflow ends with the clip URLs in the webhook response. To
auto-publish, extend after **Run summary**:

- **YouTube Shorts** — the *▶ Watch video* node already downloads the MP4
  as binary `data`; add the native **YouTube** node (Video → Upload) after
  it. Needs a YouTube OAuth2 credential.
- **Instagram / TikTok / everywhere** — pass each `videoUrl` to a scheduler
  like Blotato, Buffer or Metricool over their HTTP API; they take a public
  video URL directly, no download step.
- **Human in the loop** — a Slack or Email node sending the clip list to
  whoever approves.

They are left out of the required path on purpose so the template imports
and runs with three credentials and nothing else.
